title: Director Envelope
description: Intentional agent speech carried over the bus, peer to peer including the human. This is an A2A v1.0 compatible profile: the fields here map onto A2A v1.0 message semantics (the FIPA-ACL performative subset maps to A2A message intent), and codegen emits Go and Rust types plus validators from this one schema so the bound consumers cannot drift. Bound consumers: marvel (Go) and beadle (Rust). See contracts/README.md for the A2A mapping and the codegen targets.
$comment: Evolution rule: additive optional fields only; reserved objects stay nullable; a breaking change bumps schema_version. Authority and identity are asserted, never inferred (R-02). No credential or secret ever appears in this envelope: the credential-to-subject binding (R-77, R-85) is transport level (a NATS user or NKey per session), so the envelope carries claims, never the thing that proves them. Do not add a token or credential field here.

schema_version.description: Envelope schema version. Integer per the session-029 rule.

message_id.description: ULID: sortable, unique. Consumers dedupe on this (delivery is at least once).

correlation_id.description: Work-item thread across many messages. The loop guard keys on it (correlation_id plus performative plus recipient within a cool-down).

conversation_id.description: Reply chain. On the first message of a chain it equals message_id.

agent_id.description: The roster address, stable across restarts. Closed character class (R-76): no dot, star, angle bracket, or space, because it is interpolated into a NATS subject (director#3).

role.description: Current role. Informational only, never a routing or authorization input (R-71, R-82).

session.description: The current harness session UUID, the key (R-71). Nullable now; required once marvel sets it at spawn (R-73, R-84). Nothing derives from it yet.

principal.$comment: RESERVED. The envelope MUST validate with principal null; nothing reads it yet. Its contents are deferred (R-53) until a principal writes the bus without a human launching it (the R-77 trigger). Do not freeze claim names: kind is an open string seeded with none and launcher, and the object stays extensible.

address.$comment: agent://{team}/{id}, role://{team}/{role}, broadcast://{workspace}[/{team}]. Every segment uses the agent_id character class (R-76), so a wildcard or separator cannot be smuggled into a subject.
address.description: Where the message goes. role:// resolves to the current holder at delivery; an unresolvable address returns NOT-UNDERSTOOD to the sender.

performative.$comment: FIPA-ACL subset, the v1 cut (12 of 22). Add only on demonstrated need, which bumps schema_version. AGREE, REFUSE, FAILURE, and INFORM carry the partial-compliance distinction finding-151 asks for. NOT-UNDERSTOOD is the mandatory dead-letter behavior.

authority.$comment: A sibling of sender, never inside content (R-58, R-67). Authority is stated, never inferred (R-02). epoch is a monotonic fencing token (R-55; a NATS KV revision serves). A receiver rejects a stale epoch loudly (R-69), which is receiver logic, not schema.

strength.description: Relayed authority is provably weaker than direct (finding-151). none carries no authority.

seat.description: The authority-bearing seat, or null (the common case).

content.$comment: content never carries authority; a body that asserts its own authority is data, not authority (R-67, R-68). Anything large goes by pointer in refs, never inline (envelope cap 64 KiB).

data.description: The payload for this content type. Bounded; use refs for anything large.

refs.description: Pointers, not payload: bd:, finding:, file:, url:, pr:.

expires_at.description: Optional RFC3339 queue TTL; a stale control message dies rather than acting late.
